Upper-Triangle Adjusted Similarity Values

Source: R/metrics.R
adjusted_similarity_pairwise.Rd

Computes the full pairwise adjusted-similarity matrix for N feature sets and returns only the N\(\times\)(N-1)/2 off-diagonal upper-triangle values as a flat vector. This format is convenient for computing summary statistics (see adjusted_similarity_summary()) or for Wilcoxon/permutation tests comparing reproducibility across methods.

Usage

adjusted_similarity_pairwise(list_of_lists, nb_total_elements)

Arguments

list_of_lists

A list of character/integer vectors, one per STABL run.

nb_total_elements

Integer; total number of candidate features.

Value

Numeric vector of length N*(N-1)/2 containing the pairwise adjusted-similarity values for all unique pairs (row-major upper-triangle order, matching the Python convention).

See also

adjusted_similarity() for the pairwise function, adjusted_similarity_summary() for a one-number summary, pearson_similarity_pairwise() for an alternative chance-correction.

Examples

sets <- list(c("f1","f2","f3"), c("f2","f3","f4"), c("f1","f3","f5"))
adjusted_similarity_pairwise(sets, nb_total_elements = 10L)
#> [1] 0.36666667 0.36666667 0.03333333
